definitions.explanation: An anticipated outcome or likely result of something.
A target or goal to aim for, often in terms of time or quantity.

examples.japanese: {完成|かんせい}の{目処|めど}が{立|た}った。
{解決|かいけつ}の{目処|めど}がつかない。
examples.english: There's no prospect of a solution.

examples.japanese: {工事|こうじ}が{終|お}わる{目処|めど}はまだ{立|た}っていない。
examples.english: There's still no prospect of when the construction will finish.

examples.japanese: {就職|しゅうしょく}の{目処|めど}がついて{安心|あんしん}した。
examples.english: I was relieved when I had a prospect of finding a job.

examples.japanese: {退院|たいいん}の{目処|めど}が{立|た}たず、{家族|かぞく}は{心配|しんぱい}している。
examples.english: With no prospect of being discharged, the family is worried.

examples.japanese: 3{月|がつ}を{目処|めど}に{引|ひ}っ{越|こ}す。
examples.english: I'll move with March as my target.

examples.japanese: {来月|らいげつ}{末|まつ}を{目処|めど}に{仕上|しあ}げる。
examples.english: We'll finish with the end of next month as the target.

examples.japanese: 100{万|まん}{円|えん}を{目処|めど}に{貯金|ちょきん}している。
examples.english: I'm saving with one million yen as my goal.

examples.japanese: 1{時間|じかん}を{目処|めど}に{作業|さぎょう}を{進|すす}めてください。
examples.english: Please proceed with the work with one hour as your target.

examples.japanese: {年内|ねんない}を{目処|めど}に{新|あたら}しい{制度|せいど}を{導入|どうにゅう}する{予定|よてい}だ。
examples.english: The plan is to introduce the new system with the end of the year as the target.

notes:
ALTERNATE KANJI:
Also written as {目途|めど}, though {目処|めど} is more common.

COMMON EXPRESSIONS:
・{目処|めど}が{立|た}つ - to have a prospect (positive)
・{目処|めど}がつく - to see a prospect
・{目処|めど}がつかない - to have no prospect
・〜を{目処|めど}に - with ~ as the target

SIMILAR WORDS:
・{見通|みとお}し - outlook, perspective
・{目標|もくひょう} - goal, target
・{見込|みこ}み - prospect, expectation

USAGE:
Commonly used in business and project planning contexts.
